title: Assessing Motor Cortical Excitability with Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
author: Ortega-Robles, Cantillo-Negrete, et al.

steps.title: Activate and configure equipment
steps.instruction: Turn on and correctly configure all devices required for the experiment, including the TMS stimulator, EMG recording system, and neuronavigation platform.

substeps.instruction: Power on the TMS unit and verify coil integrity.
Power on the EMG amplifier and connect surface electrodes to the target muscle.
Start the neuronavigation system and load the subject’s MRI (if used).
Check that all devices communicate properly and are set to the default operating parameters.

steps.title: Prepare the subject
steps.instruction: Instruct the participant to relax, keep the hands in a stable comfortable position, and minimize any movement throughout the session.

substeps.instruction: Explain the importance of staying relaxed and still.
Seat the subject comfortably with forearms supported.
Place the hands on a padded surface to prevent drift.

steps.title: Calculate Resting Motor Threshold (RMT)
steps.instruction: Determine the subject’s RMT using the ATH‑tool adaptive algorithm, which provides rapid and accurate threshold estimation with fewer stimuli than traditional methods.

substeps.instruction: Launch the ATH‑tool application on the controlling computer.
Select the adaptive RMT protocol and set the initial stimulus intensity range.
Deliver single TMS pulses while monitoring EMG for motor‑evoked potentials.
Allow the algorithm to converge on the intensity that elicits MEPs ≥ 50 µV in at least 5 of 10 trials.
Record the final RMT value displayed by the software.

steps.title: Document RMT values
steps.instruction: Immediately record the RMT obtained from the ATH‑tool in the experimental log for later use in setting stimulation intensities.

steps.title: Confirm protocol adherence
steps.instruction: Verify that each of the preceding steps has been completed exactly as described to ensure a reliable RMT measurement.

steps.title: Initiate planned intervention
steps.instruction: After the baseline (pre‑intervention) measurement, begin the chosen intervention intended to modify cortical excitability (e.g., repetitive TMS, pharmacological agent, or neuro‑rehabilitation protocol).

steps.title: Perform post‑intervention MEP measurement
steps.instruction: Record motor‑evoked potentials after the intervention using the same procedure as the baseline measurement, adjusting the number of trials according to the expected duration of after‑effects.

substeps.instruction: Set the inter‑stimulus interval to 6 seconds.
For an rTMS protocol, acquire approximately 150 MEPs (≈15 minutes of recording).
If a different intervention is used, ensure the total number of MEPs is equal to or greater than the baseline count.

steps.title: Analyze pre‑ and post‑intervention data
steps.instruction: Compare the series of pre‑ and post‑intervention MEP amplitudes to assess changes in cortical excitability using the chosen statistical or analytical method.
